Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — pricing/latency tradeoffs

Hi Ari — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on pricing/qualification.

Recap (from our call):
- Expected traffic: 50M–150M tokens/month initially, with peak inference spikes during batch runs (end of quarter reporting) up to ~10k concurrent short calls.
- Primary workload: realtime conversational flows (avg 120 tokens/request) + a smaller async batch rerank pipeline (~1B tokens/month, lower latency tolerance).
- Latency target (customer-facing chat): p95 <= 250ms ideally; SLO-driven needs may accept 400ms during spikes.

Pricing / unit economics discussion items:
- Your target blended spend: $3k–10k/month initially; target $/1M tokens you mentioned is in the $25–140 range, depending on latency.
- Tradeoffs we discussed: lower-latency (dedicated/smaller batch windows + streaming) increases unit cost; batching + KV caching reduces cost but increases tail latency.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm monthly token breakdown (conversational vs batch) — I captured 70/30 but want your confirmation.
2) Vivek and I will model two scenarios (hosted standard tier + streaming vs dedicated reserved capacity with batching/quantization). We’ll return: estimated $/1M tokens, expected p95 latency, and recommended config.
3) If that looks good, we’ll prepare a formal quote and a 30-day pilot plan (capacity + SLA targets).

I attached a short pricing tier doc and a sample SLA draft for reference.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

Looping in some quick engineering notes (hi Ari). High level options that map to the tradeoffs we discussed:

Option A — Hosted standard (streaming + small batch)
- Good for fast time-to-value, handles 60M conversational tokens without reserved commit.
- Estimated p95 chat latency: 180–300ms depending on model choice & prompt length.
- Estimated blended unit cost: $28–$38 / 1M tokens (with streaming and modest batching).
- Pros: no infra commitment; quick pilot. Cons: higher unit cost at scale, limited ability to tune quantization.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (batch-optimized + KV caching + int8 quantization)
- Best for large batch volume (~900M tokens/month) and predictable throughput.
- Estimated p95 chat latency (with routing policies to reserve nodes for critical flows): 120–220ms for critical routes, 300–450ms for lower-priority routes.
- Estimated blended unit cost: $9–$20 / 1M tokens depending on commit, batching window, and quantization profile.
- Pros: lower unit economics at scale, deterministic throughput. Cons: commit required; initial setup time.

Option C — Hybrid (reserved for critical flows + hosted for general chat)
- Reserve a small pool for the checkout fraud path (p95 <= 200ms) and use hosted for the rest.
- Blended unit cost estimated: $18–$27 / 1M tokens and meets the SLOs for critical flows.

We’ll produce a cost model spreadsheet with assumptions (batch window, avg tokens per call, KV cache hit-rate, expected concurrency) and include sensitivity analysis for SLO thresholds.

Next steps: Marissa — we’ll draft the model and a recommended pilot (30 days, 2-week ramp, SLA p95 targets) and share by EOD Monday. Rishi — we may need pricing exception language for pilot discounts (Ari's $5k budget).

—Vivek
